A boundary value passes one comparison and fails the other, so a length or count is off by one.
A size is read as signed, and a caller can make it negative so the check flips.
Two sizes are added and the sum is allowed to wrap or exceed the destination.
A conversion drops the high part of a length, and a later copy uses the short value.
A check mixes characters, bytes, and code points as if they were the same unit.
Caller text is concatenated into a command string that a shell will parse.
Caller text is concatenated into a query that a database parser will execute.
Caller text is placed into markup or a template without encoding for that context.
A path join discards the base when the second part is absolute.
A path is checked for a parent segment, then normalised only after the check.
An allow-list sees an unresolved path, and a later segment leaves the intended root.
A directory confinement check happens before a symlink is followed.
Bytes from the caller are restored with a loader that can run constructors.
A configuration parser trusts a type tag that the caller included in the document.
An archive entry name is used as an output path and is not confined to the destination.
A structured-document parser fetches external entities or remote schema documents.
A template engine evaluates expressions in a document that is only partly trusted.
A redirect target is taken from the request and is not limited to known hosts.
The server fetches a URL the caller chose.
A host allow-list can be confused by an alternate address spelling or an extra userinfo marker.
A secret comparison stops at the first differing character.
A token is accepted under more than one algorithm, including one that treats a public value as the key.
A payload is acted on before its signature is checked.
A password or key is stored with a fast hash and no salt.
A security decision uses a predictable random source.
A cipher repeats a nonce, or uses a mode that leaks when two blocks are equal.
An error path returns success, or a default of allow.
A failed check raises, the handler swallows it, and execution continues.
A missing authentication step is treated as an anonymous user who still has rights.
An authorisation decision trusts an id the client sent instead of the one stored with the session.
A cache key omits the tenant or the user, so one caller can read another's value.
A privilege flag defaults to enabled when the field is absent.
A resource is checked, then used after a point where another actor can change it.
A read-modify-write of shared state is not atomic, or two locks are taken in opposite orders.
A limit is enforced on one entry point and skipped on another that reaches the same function.
A regular expression over caller text can take time that grows much faster than the input.
A decoder recurses on nested input with no depth limit.
A hash table or set is filled with keys the caller chooses, with no cap on how many.
One comparison normalises Unicode and the other does not, so lookalike strings pass.
Case-folding or an encoding is applied to only part of an identifier.
A filter removes one dangerous marker and leaves a second copy of it in place.
Removing characters joins the surrounding text into a new dangerous token.
A file is created with the process umask where a private mode was required.
A temporary file is opened, then reopened by name, so the name can be swapped.
A log line includes raw request data, and control characters can forge extra records.
A secret is baked into source, a default argument, or an example the runtime still loads.
A caller-controlled count is used as a slice or a repeat with no upper bound.
A binary floating value is used where an exact decimal total is required, so sums drift.
An identifier is recycled after deletion while other records still point at it.
Equality uses a field the caller can set, and that bypasses an immutable id.
A parser accepts a duplicate key and keeps the one the later check did not expect.
A comment, quote, or escape stays open across a newline, so the next line changes meaning.
A decompression step expands input by a ratio that is not bounded.
A state-changing request is accepted because a cookie is sent and no separate token is checked.
A navigation target or refresh is built from a query parameter.
A header value is split on a newline the caller included.
A privilege drop happens after the privileged work, or is skipped on one branch.
Versions or ranges are compared with string order.
A missing field skips a check that a present field would have failed.
A retry repeats an action that already took effect.
A collection taken from the input is processed in full before its length is checked, so one request costs work in proportion to a size the caller picks.
Input is decoded, split or decompressed before its size is checked, so memory in proportion to the caller's input is allocated first.
